title: Assembling level adjunctions into strict-system images
statement: Under the sites, ring and geometric-adjunction hypotheses of [def-pur-coefficient-system-image-data], a left exact L admits an ordinary image package CoefficientSystemOrdinaryImage on the strict coefficient systems. The inverse and direct functors are formed from the normalized level functors and their scalar-restriction comparisons. Their adjunction is exactly the componentwise level transposition, and the inverse image is additive and exact. No derived category, coefficient regularity or completeness is assumed.

source.place: Zheng Construction 4.1 and the paragraph before Lemma 4.10: applying the geometric morphism levelwise to the ringed sequence topos.

proof.text: Choose the level lifts, adjunctions and restriction comparisons. On systems set (FM)n=Fn(Mn) and (GN)n=Gn(Nn), with transitions obtained by mapping the original transition and composing with the corresponding restriction comparison. Their naturality proves compatibility for mapped system morphisms.

Transpose each component of a system morphism. The restriction-transpose equation identifies the two transition equations, so these component transposes give inverse natural Hom bijections. Construct the system adjunction with that Hom equivalence. Addition is detected componentwise; the right adjoint is additive too.

Evaluation functors are exact. They jointly reflect isomorphisms because a componentwise inverse family satisfies the transition equation by cancellation. Apply the exactness-detection square to the componentwise exact inverse images. The evaluation isomorphisms and required transition and transpose normalizations are the identity comparisons by construction.

mathlib_searches.verdict: The ordinary continuous-site pullback API is useful but does not supply the arbitrary geometric morphism, independent site universes, constant coefficient normalization and strict-system transition comparison here.
